newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker in range trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker in range trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended weaker in range-bound, quiet trade on Tuesday as banks concentrated on meeting commercial requirements of clients, traders said.
The peso closed at 28.15 to the dollar from the previous 28.
The central bank continued to be in the market, selling about $5.5 million at 28.30/28.02, they said.
Market volume was light at $43 million as the peso traded in the band of 28.02/28.47.
Traders said the peso continue to settle down after its de facto devaluation over a week ago.
"Spreads between bid and offer have gone down. That signals some form of stability in the market," a foreign bank dealer said.
Earlier, President Fidel Ramos expressed satisfaction over the way the peso behaved in recent days.

He said the peso's recovery was because "the economic fundamentals in the Philippines are very, very sound and we must not be equated to other countries that may be suffering from the same speculative attacks."
Traders said they expect the peso to stay in a range of 28/28.50 on Wednesday.
